title: Like Decimal Maker
description: Count decimal places, sort like from unlike, and write zeros after the point to make decimals like, giving a whole number its point first.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit.

writeup.why: Tell like decimals from unlike decimals by counting decimal places, and change unlike decimals, whole numbers included, into like decimals by writing zeros after the point.
writeup.look: Decimal cards with their points in one line, Like and Unlike trays under them, a tray of violet zero chips at the right, and a hundred grid under a card on the third phase.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Like Decimal Maker' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x sixty-four, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: how many decimal places the longest card has, so the child sees the target for the others. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x sixty-four, y 202. The cards stand one under another from y 240 in the left half of the working area, each 420 wide and 70 tall, their large near-black points all on one vertical line at x 330, the digits deep blue. The count of places sits at the right end of each card in amber once Count places is tapped. The Like decimals and Unlike decimals trays stand side by side along y 600, each 400 by 110 and labelled in ink. The tray of violet zero chips, each labelled Added zero, runs down the right of the working area at x 1000. On the third phase a hundred grid, or a strip in tenths, 300 across, sits under the card being changed at x 560, y 380, and keeps its shading as the zeros are added. On the fourth the Point first button sits at x 560, y 250, and a point it writes is violet. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is twelve number keys three across with a point key, for setting a decimal with up to three places or a whole number, or for typing a like decimal into the answer slot. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the tools of this chapter share them. A decimal or fraction the question gives is deep blue, with the shaded parts that show it. The result the working reaches, a decimal, a fraction, a sum, a difference or what is left, is green, with its shaded parts. Ten of one place traded for one of the next, a carry in adding or a trade in taking away, is vermilion. A zero written after the point to line decimals up is violet, and so is the point written after a whole number before those zeros. The part taken away, used or poured out is rose. The digit, place or step being worked on now, and the first place where two decimals differ, are amber. A zero holding a place open inside a number is grey, and nothing else on the stage is ever grey. An unshaded part stays warm white inside its near-black outline, the decimal point is near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength rather than turning grey. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each of those readings survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label, Given, Answer, Carry, Trade, Added zero, Taken away, Left or Place holder, before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The card shows the last set of cards made like, their points in one line and the added zeros in violet.

phases.win: every card shows two places, and the set settles on the Like decimals tray
phases.does: taps Count places and reads the count at the right of each card
phases.goal: decimals with the same number of decimal places are like decimals
phases.says: Count only the digits after the point. Do the counts match?
phases.check: Away from the screen: how many decimal places does a length written with two digits after the point have?
phases.feels: the digits after the point lighting up and being counted
phases.hands: Write three decimals on slips. Underline the digits after each point and count them. Put slips with the same count in one pile.
phases.tries: First rung: count the places of one card. Second rung: count the next. Third rung: the same task with two cards, before the full set returns.

wrong.why: decimals that look close in size seem to belong together

phases.does: drags zero chips onto the end of 3.8 until both have three places
phases.goal: zeros written at the end, after the point, make decimals like and do not change the value

phases.check: Away from the screen: do eight tenths and eighty hundredths shade the same part of a grid?
phases.feels: zeros settling at the end while the shading does not move
phases.hands: Shade eight columns of a hundred grid and write the decimal in tenths and then in hundredths. Check that the shading is the same both times.
phases.tries: First rung: count the places of the longest card. Second rung: add one zero after the point of a shorter card. Third rung: the same task with two cards, before three return.

wrong.why: the zeros seem to fill a gap wherever there is room
wrong.move: drops a zero chip inside the decimal, before its last digit
wrong.screen: the chip slides back to the end after the last digit, and the grid shows what the other spot would have done to the shading

wrong.why: adding zeros feels like something done to every card

writeup.delight: On the third phase, as each violet zero chip settles after the point, the hundred grid under the card gives a small shiver and its cells redraw finer, yet the shaded part stays exactly where it was.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with the cards standing one under another, their points in one line and nothing lit. On the first two phases the Like decimals and Unlike decimals trays wait under them. On the third the violet zero chips wait at the right and a hundred grid lies under the shorter card. On the fourth a whole number card with no point stands beside a decimal, and the Point first button is unlit. One thing moves, once: the Count places button, the first zero chip or the whole number card gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line, and a finger on it is the whole way in.
writeup.freePlay: Any decimals and whole numbers, sorted, made like with zero chips, and given their points first. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on counting places, like and unlike decimals, zeros after the point and whole numbers.

observations.why: decimal places are the digits after the point.
observations.soWhat: decimals with the same number of decimal places are like decimals.
observations.observe: The count of places never included the digits before the point.

observations.why: their numbers of decimal places differ.
observations.soWhat: decimals with different numbers of decimal places are unlike decimals.
observations.observe: Cards with different counts would not settle on the Like tray.

observations.why: a zero at the end after the point adds an empty place, worth nothing.
observations.soWhat: zeros written at the end, after the point, make decimals like and do not change the value.
observations.observe: The grid under the card kept its shading as each zero was added after the point.

observations.why: with no point, the zero lands in the ones place and every digit moves up a place.
observations.soWhat: a whole number gets its point first, and zeros are added only after the point.
observations.observe: A zero chip dropped straight onto a whole number made the card jump, and slid off.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: The digits before each point fade, the digits after it light and are counted, and the like set settles on the Like tray.
Phase 2: The counts of places stand side by side and the pair settles on the Unlike tray; equal strips show 5.20, 5.2 and 5.200 have one value.
Phase 3: Zeros put inside slide back to the end, missing zeros settle after the last digit, and the grid keeps its shading.
Phase 4: Zeros stuck straight onto a whole number slide off, the point is written after the ones digit, then the zeros settle.

voice.rules: Spoken on opening, as each phase begins, on each question, on a miss and on the summary page. Every line is printed in the bubble, numbers as words, by the device's own voice (Indian English first). Muting keeps the child's place; unmuting speaks on from the word it reached. If the browser refuses speech until a tap, the first line waits behind a Tap to start cover.

guide.playsOn: none: an Udgam tool opens straight on its phase; the phase's teach lines are spoken first, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

toolQuestions.source: props.questions ?? props.additionalProps?.questions is read; the authored rows below keep their stage (fitHost returns null).

items.planQuestion: How many decimal places do 6.02, 13.47 and 0.93 have? Are they like decimals?

question.en: How many decimal places do 6.02, 13.47 and 0.93 have? Are they like decimals?

items.planAnswer: Each has two decimal places, so they are like decimals

items.planQuestion: How many decimal places does 14.306 have?

question.en: How many decimal places does 14.306 have?

items.planAnswer: 3, because three digits come after the point

items.planQuestion: Which two of 3.14, 31.4 and 0.72 are like decimals?

question.en: Which two of 3.14, 31.4 and 0.72 are like decimals?

items.planAnswer: 3.14 and 0.72. Each has two decimal places, and 31.4 has one
No. 7.1 has one decimal place and 7.105 has three, so they are unlike decimals

items.planQuestion: Are 0.6 and 0.66 like or unlike decimals?

question.en: Are 0.6 and 0.66 like or unlike decimals?

items.planAnswer: Unlike. 0.6 has one decimal place and 0.66 has two

items.planQuestion: Do 5.20, 5.2 and 5.200 have the same value? Are they like decimals?

question.en: Do 5.20, 5.2 and 5.200 have the same value? Are they like decimals?

items.planAnswer: They have the same value, because zeros at the end after the point change nothing. They are unlike decimals, with two, one and three decimal places

ask.en: Add zeros to make them like

question.en: Now three cards: 0.3, 0.46 and 0.127. Line them all up the same way.

items.planQuestion: Write the whole number 12 with three decimal places.

question.en: Write the whole number 12 with three decimal places.

items.planAnswer: 12.000. Write the point first, then three zeros after it

question.en: Now 6, 2.8 and 0.315 together. Which one needs a point first?

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page; finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }
